and he took captives, and plundered, and went out to Macedonia.
And when he reached the region of Synnada,
winter and heavy snow overtook him.
And he sent to a certain Greek woman whose name was Maria,
who was ruling over the fortress of Synnada,
and asked of her that the forces of the Turks might enter into her city and villages,
so that they might purchase provisions for themselves.
And with difficulty she permitted [them],
after he threatened her that he would cut down the trees and uproot the vineyards and gardens in her region.
Now King Diogenes gathered a large army,
and went forth from the region of Armenia with great pride,
and came against Manzikert.
And he drove out the Sultan's men from it,
yet he did not kill them,
and took control of it.
And when the Sultan heard [this],
he turned his attention toward the Romans.
And because the Turks were few in number,
Sultan Alp Arslan became afraid,
and sent an envoy to Diogenes, a certain man from the grandees whose name was Sawtakin, that they might make peace,
and give oaths to one another,
and that each one should return to his own country.
Diogenes, however, became arrogant in himself and said:
"Now that I have emptied my treasuries and gathered all these forces,
and victory is mine,
shall I turn back? You have nothing from me except the sword!"
Then God,
praise be to His grace,
He Who humbles the proud,
strengthened the Sultan.
And he prepared his forces,
and spoke encouraging words to them,
and cast the bow and arrows from his hands,
and put on his armor,
and took a mace and a spear in his hand,
and tied up his horse's tail and mounted.
And all the Turks likewise did the same.
And they rushed upon the Romans on Friday at the time of noon between Akhlat and Manzikert,
and they raised a mighty shout,
and mingled with them.
And terror fell upon the Romans,
and they began to flee after many of them were killed,
and others were taken prisoner.
And at evening time, a certain eunuch among the Turkish grandees whose name was Gawhara came and said to the Sultan:
"One of my slaves said
that he has captured the king of the Romans,
and behold, he is with him."
Now as for this slave,
when the horsemen were being mustered,
the emir of the wardrobe had despised him,
and did not write down his rations.
